purpose: Help a desktop user import a personal document archive, index it locally, organize it with tags, find an item, and open the selected result without losing work when imports fail or duplicates are found.

screens.purpose: Show the empty library or indexed collection, expose import and tagging controls, and preserve the user's current selection.
Report real import and indexing progress, announce status changes, and keep failure and retry controls in keyboard order.
Accept title or tag searches, show result counts or a recoverable no-results state, and allow opening a selected result.
Open the selected indexed item while retaining a clear keyboard path back to the search results.

actions.label: Begin local indexing after validating selected files
Finish indexing and expose the collection
Add a tag to the selected indexed item
Report a failed import without changing the existing library
Retry the failed import from the preserved file selection
Identify an already indexed item before creating another record
Keep the canonical item and preserve its existing metadata
Report that the current query has no matches
Clear or revise the query and return focus to search
Return from the open item to the prior result selection

constraints: Use PowerShell 7 with PresentationFramework and XAML for a Windows desktop WPF application.
Use one shared state and action model for UI, smoke, and render paths so visible status corresponds to actual behavior.
Keep archive indexing local and do not imply cloud upload, synchronization, or network access.
Do not overwrite existing item metadata when duplicate content is detected.
Preserve the selected files and existing library when an import fails so retry is reversible and safe.
Provide keyboard navigation, visible focus, accessible names, status announcements, sufficient contrast, and reduced-motion behavior.
Show the mouse librarian only in empty-library, indexing, and recovery states.
In action states remove the default chest V/U and use exactly one body-connected action-hand pair touching the real book, card, index, or retry control.
Derive interface styling only from the archive workflow, Windows desktop conventions, and accessibility evidence; bundled character and composition images provide no UI-style authority.
Keep generated, tested, run, rendered, visually checked, and accepted gates independent until evidence exists.
